title: Karmic tail 18-6-15 in the destiny matrix: the “Dark Magician”, spells, the chain and a magic that lets go

seo.title: Karmic tail 18-6-15, the “Dark Magician”, in the destiny matrix
seo.description: 18-6-15 is the tail where charm turns into a chain. A ten-second date check, the Empress at everyone’s centre, Faust and Margarete, and eight practices.

short: 18-6-15 is the karmic tail that popular destiny matrix readings call the “Dark Magician” (less often, the “Black Magician”). The past-life legend tells of a person with secret knowledge and power over people who used that power for themselves: cast love spells, bent other people’s will, kept them close. The numbers say nothing about past lives or witchcraft. But you can recognise the tail’s scenario without any candles. The person knows how to charm: they sense what others want and show them what they want to see. Charm grows into a bond — love, friendship, work, students. Then the bond turns into a chain. It is held in place by control, jealousy, gifts, being indispensable — or the person cannot get out of it themselves. The Moon (18) opens the circle: spells and images in reflected light. The Lovers (6) keep it going: a union made by moonlight. The Devil (15) sits at the root: the chain, and the task of learning a strength that does not hold anyone. About the figure who towers over the chained pair on this card, Waite wrote the key line: he is not to be their master for ever, and “even now, he is also a bondsman”. Everyone with this tail has the Empress at the centre of the chart — in Waite’s words, “desire and the wings thereof”. The tail is rare and young: one in 132 people born in the 20th century has it, and one in 31 of those born since 2000. Its main question is how to influence without binding, and to love without owning.

sections.h2: Do you have the 18-6-15 tail? A ten-second check
paragraphs: The tail depends entirely on one number: the sum of the first three arcana of the matrix. You don’t need a calculator.

ol: **Day arcanum** — your day of birth. If it is greater than 22, add its digits: 23 → 5, 27 → 9, 30 → 3, 31 → 4.
**Year arcanum** — the sum of the digits of the year. If it comes out above 22, add the digits again: 1985 → 23 → 5, 1987 → 25 → 7, and 2003 → 5.

paragraphs: Add the three numbers. If you get **exactly 15**, you have 18-6-15. Any other sum means you don’t have this tail: there is no other way to get it.

ul: 05.07.1974: 5 + 7 + 21 = 33 → not this one. It is 18-6-6: the same entry and the same middle, but the Lovers again at the root.
09.09.1986: 9 + 9 + 6 = 24 → not this one. It is 9-15-6: the same Lovers and Devil and the same centre, but the roles have swapped places.
06.02.1977: 6 + 2 + 6 = 14 → not this one. Just one less, and the tail is already completely different: 6-20-14.

paragraphs: If your chart has already been calculated, it is even simpler. Look at the bottom corner, point D, the “karmic task”. If it shows 15, you have 18-6-15, with no exceptions.

Why this works. The sum 15 goes straight into the bottom corner of the chart: D = 15, and since the number is not above 22, it is not reduced. No other sum gives 15. The three numbers of a date add up to at most 56, and none of the numbers from 23 to 56 has digits that add up to 15. The centre E is the same sum plus the corner: 15 + 15 = 30 → 3. The entry M = D + E = 15 + 3 = 18. The middle N = D + M = 15 + 18 = 33 → 6. This was checked by going through all 73,414 days from 1900 to 2100.
Read the scheme from the bottom up:

head: Point
Arcanum
How it is derived
rows: sum of the three numbers, exactly 15

paragraphs: Sums whose digits add up to 6 give three neighbouring tails. People often mix them up:
The same arithmetic leads to facts you won’t find in popular readings:

ul: **It is rare.** From 1900 to 2100, 18-6-15 falls on 843 dates out of 73,414 — about one in 87 (1.15%). That puts it 21st out of 26 possible tails. Only 6-20-14 and four very rare tails are less common: 3-13-10, 21-10-7, 9-18-9 and 6-14-8.

**It is the only tail with the Devil at the root.** The Devil appears in four more of the 26 tails, but there it is the entry (15-5-8, 15-8-11, 15-20-5) or the middle (9-15-6). Only here is it the task, that is, the root.
**It is the tail of the 2000s kids.** The earlier the year of birth, the rarer it is:

paragraphs: Among people born in the 20th century, one in 132 has this tail, and it ranks 21st by frequency. Among those born since 2000, it is one in 31, and it climbs to 17th place. In 2000 it went to one person in eighteen, making it the fourth most common tail of that year. More than half of all dates with this tail from 1900 to today belong to people born since 2000.

The reason is arithmetic. The day arcanum and the month together give at least 2, so the year arcanum cannot be greater than 13. Years of the 20th century usually have a large arcanum: 1940 → 14, 1948 → 22. That would leave the day and the month to make up one or less, which is impossible. The tail appears only in years whose digit sum went past 22 and reduced to a small number: 1949 → 23 → 5, 1985 → 23 → 5, 1999 → 28 → 10. Years of the 2000s have a small arcanum (2000 → 2, 2005 → 7), and dozens of day-and-month combinations bring the sum up to 15.

ul: **Nineteen years without a single date.** From 2 January 1930 to 8 January 1949, not one person was born with the 18-6-15 tail. In the 36 years from 1913 to 1948, only four dates got it: 2 January and 1 February 1920, 1 January 1921 and 1 January 1930. Later there are years without it too: 1950–1957, 1960–1966, 1970–1975, 1980–1984 and 1990–1993. If you were born in 1991, for example, you cannot have this tail.

**It is a tail of winter and spring.** One holder in five was born in January, and more than half between January and March. From October to December the tail has fallen on only eleven dates since 1900, and all of them are in 2000–2020. The last was 1 October 2020; the next will not come until 2 October 2100. In two centuries there is exactly one December date: 1 December 2000. The reason is the same arithmetic: the month number is part of the sum, and with month 12 only 3 is left for the day and the year. That is possible only with day 1 and the year 2000.

**15-6-18 is the same tail, read from the corner.** If you see 15, 6 and 18 on the bottom ray of your chart, you are reading the same tail from the outer corner towards the centre. The roles stay the same: the Moon is the entry, the Devil the root. There is no separate 15-6-18 tail: 18 in the bottom corner only comes from a sum of 18, which gives centre 9 and the tail 9-9-18. And the triple 18-6-15 itself does not appear anywhere in the matrix except on the bottom ray: not in the relationship line, not in the money line, not in the talent line.

sections.h2: Why this tail is called the “Dark Magician”
paragraphs: Popular interpretations explain the name with a past-life legend. The person supposedly had deep secret knowledge — magic, occult practices — and power over other people’s will. They used it for themselves: love spells, hexes, curses, suggestion, domination. In some retellings they were a powerful priest, in others a “grey eminence” behind a strong ruler. There is also a version without magic: a dissolute life, infidelity and love intrigues.

That is where today’s claims about the tail come from. Magnetism and charisma: people are drawn to such a person “for no visible reason”. A gift for influence — and a tendency to manipulate, often without realising it. A wish to control everything and to “rescue” people who never asked. Jealousy and possessiveness. A tendency towards addictions — to people, pleasures, things. And a split attitude to magic: either a burning attraction or an almost animal fear. Some add the feeling of a “sleeping giant”: huge strength inside, stagnation outside. The legend cannot be checked. The digits of a birth date say nothing about the past, or about whether a person practises magic. But as a metaphor the legend is precise. This is how someone lives whose main tool is influence and whose main temptation is to hold on.
What matters more is this. The magic in this tail was not invented by popular readings: it is in the cards themselves.

**The Moon.** In Waite’s list of divinatory meanings, the Moon has “darkness”, “deception” and “occult forces”. Benebell Wen calls the Moon the signifier for society’s “magi, priest, or shaman”. And she adds an image that fits this tail better than any definition of magic. The moon pulls on the water, and that makes the tides. When the Moon appears in a reading, Wen writes, there is an “external invisible force” pulling on the person. A spell is exactly that: an invisible pull.

**The Devil.** Waite retells, with irony, a claim by Éliphas Lévi, a 19th-century French occultist. Lévi affirmed that the horned figure on this card “is occult science and magic”. Waite himself does not accept this reading. For him the card signifies “the Dweller on the Threshold without the Mystical Garden” — the one who stands outside when those who have eaten the forbidden fruit are driven out of it.

Now take Waite’s descriptions of two cards and put them side by side. What follows is our comparison, not his conclusion. The Magician raises a wand to the sky with his right hand and points to the earth with his left. According to Waite, this sign shows “the descent of grace, virtue and light” from things above to things below. The Devil’s right hand is raised too, but Waite calls this gesture “the reverse of that benediction which is given by the Hierophant”. In his left hand is a torch “inverted towards the earth”. On the Devil’s belly is the sign of Mercury, and Mercury is the Magician’s planet (Wen says so too). On his forehead is a reversed pentagram. The magician’s pose, the magician’s sign — and everything turned downwards. If you look for a “dark magician” in the deck, he is drawn on the fifteenth card. And Wen supplies the “dark”: on the Devil card, “everything behind the beast and Lovers is black”.

But Waite’s most important line about this card is not about magic. A man and a woman are chained to the altar the Devil stands on: chains run from a ring to their necks, “as if Adam and Eve after the Fall”. And then: “he who is exalted above them is not to be their master for ever. Even now, he is also a bondsman, sustained by the evil that is in him and blind to the liberty of service.” The dark magician of the legend is the least free figure on his own card. For the tail, the main conclusion follows: in the “Dark Magician” scenario, nobody is free. The one who holds is held too, and those who are held are holding him.

There is also a detail in Waite that sounds almost like a joke. The chained figures on the card are tailed, “to signify the animal nature”. But “there is human intelligence in the faces”, Waite writes. At the root of this karmic tail stands the only one of its cards on which people literally have tails. And in Waite it comes with a “but”: there is a tail, but the face is human.

sections.h2: The dark magician’s dictionary: Russian remembers that love is witchcraft
paragraphs: In Russian, people talk about falling in love with words that once meant witchcraft, deceit and captivity, and don’t notice it.

ul: **Ocharovat** (to charm) — from chary, spells, that is, witchcraft.
**Obvorozhit** and **privorozhit** (to bewitch, to bind with a love spell) — from vorozhit: to work magic, to tell fortunes.
**Obayanie** (charm) — from the old obayat: to bewitch with words, to cast a spoken spell (the same root as in bayat, to speak).
**Prelest** (loveliness), **prelstit** and **obolstit** (to allure, to seduce) — from lest in its old sense of “deceit, cunning”. In church language prelest still means spiritual delusion.
**Soblazn** (temptation) — from blaznit: to lead into error. In dialects, blaznitsya still means “to be seeing things”.
**Plenitelny** (captivating) and **plenit** (to captivate) — from plen, captivity.
**Privyazannost** (attachment) — from privyazat, to tie up.

paragraphs: English does the same: the word glamour once meant “a magic spell”.

Look at how this dictionary spreads across the cards of the tail. Spells, fortune-telling and things that only seem to be there belong to the Moon. The love it all starts for belongs to the Lovers. Captivity and being tied belong to the Devil. The whole 18-6-15 tail already lies in ordinary words about love.

Etymology proves nothing about numbers. But it does show that the “Dark Magician” describes not a rare occult gift but an ordinary human one: being liked, drawing people in, making them think about you. Plenty of people have charm. The 18-6-15 tail asks about something else: what you do next — open the door or lock it.

sections.h2: How the circle works: spells, union, chain
paragraphs: **1. Entry: the Moon — spells.** The scenario starts with a fine sense for the invisible. A person with 18-6-15 reads the mood of a room in a second. They know what to say, to whom, and when to keep quiet. They see what someone is missing — and become it. Wen writes of the Moon that intuition is strong here, and that the person has “hidden abilities to harness both tame elements and wild elements”. In life this looks like a gift for being a mirror in which the other person sees the best version of themselves.

Waite describes the light that falls on everything here. For him the Moon is “life of the imagination apart from life of the spirit”, and the way is lit by “only reflected light”. Spells work with images. The other person falls in love not with you but with what you reflected back to them. And the light falls both ways. Someone who charms easily is just as easily charmed: they fall under the spell of a bright person, a teacher, an idea.

On the same card Wen has a crayfish crawling out of the water. It stands for “a sense of needing to feel protected, and thus forming the tough outer shell”. And, at the same time, for “a profound vulnerability that the Seeker is trying to conceal from others”. Charm is the most elegant shell there is. As long as people like you, nobody sees you.

**2. Mechanism: the Lovers — a union by moonlight.** Charm leads to union. It can be love, friendship, a partnership, a team, students, followers. Wen writes of the Lovers: “a strong feeling of paradise, at least in the beginning”. And she warns at once: “under every flower a serpent coiled”, and bliss can quickly become tragedy. In Waite’s list of divinatory meanings, the first word for the Lovers is “attraction”.

The trouble with a union made by moonlight is that both people chose an image. And the person with 18-6-15 knows it, or at least suspects it. They are loved for a reflection, and reflections break. So the union has to be guarded rather than lived. Wen notes that the Lovers carry “an underlying theme of indecision”: the choice was never made in daylight. And she explains the difference between the two lower cards of the tail in a single line: “Key 6 is about one choice. Key 15 is about being led astray.”
**3. Root: the Devil — the chain.** Where there is fear of loss, chains appear. They come in different kinds:

ul: control: knowing where they are, who they are with, what they write and what they are thinking about;
jealousy that grows not from facts but from things imagined;
help with a hook: solving their problems, giving them money, finding them a job, introducing them to the right people — so that leaving becomes unthinkable;
rescue nobody asked for: “I know better what you need”;
a debt nobody agreed to: “after everything I’ve done for you”.

paragraphs: Sometimes it is the other way round: a person is being held and does not leave, even though they are suffocating. Wen calls the Devil “bondage to the material and superficial, preference for instant gratification over delayed gratification”. And she says it plainly: if the Seeker is in a relationship, “it could be an unhealthy one that is chaining him or her down”. She also links the card with “despotism and enslavement”. But she warns that the card does not mean the Seeker is “entirely to blame”.

Waite has a passing word of praise that is worth more to this tail than many pages. Talking about different pictures of the Devil, he mentions the version of the French occultist Papus. There, instead of small demons, there are “naked human beings, male and female, who are yoked only to each other”. Waite calls this an “improved symbolism”. A chain doesn’t need a third party. The bond between two people can itself become the chain.

**4. Repetition.** The chain chafes. Someone leaves — with a scene or in silence. Or the person with 18-6-15 leaves first, “before I get dumped”. What remains is a bitter conclusion, and it comes in two kinds. The first: “you can’t trust people, you have to keep hold of them”. The second: “I am dangerous, I’d better not get close to anyone”. Then comes a new meeting. The spell works again, again someone has to be held on to, and each new circle starts with stronger spells and ends with a tighter chain.

Imagine a woman of twenty-four. People she has known for half an hour tell her their secrets. At a party she meets a man, and within an hour she understands what he is missing: being understood. She gives him that. Two months later he says nobody has ever understood him like this. Six months later she knows his schedule, his friends and his mother’s birthday. She has rewritten his CV and lent him money for a course. She can see when he was last online. If he replies later than usual, she rereads their chat and comes up with three theories about what his “ok” means. When he plans a weekend away with friends, she forbids nothing. She just gets sad, and he stays. Six months after that he says: “With you it’s like living under a glass dome.” She answers: “But I did everything for you.” That is true — and that is the chain. In her next relationship she will be even more indispensable.
Now swap the roles. He may have the same tail too — the one who stays even though he has long been suffocating, because “nobody has ever understood me like this”.

sections.h2: The Enchanter, the Captive and the Renouncer: one and the same tail
paragraphs: Popular readings usually describe one of two people: the manipulator, or the one who is afraid of magic and of their own power. In fact these are modes of one scenario, and there is a third.

head: The Enchanter
The Captive
The Renouncer
The tail worked through
rows: off the card — in the Empress’s garden
“I don’t need anyone”, “all this magic is dangerous nonsense”
“I want you to be happy — with me or without me”
give themselves to whoever charmed them
hide it and forbid it to themselves
put it into their work and into closeness
constant vigilance: what you hold, you have to guard
a strength that never got used

paragraphs: The modes take turns. After a hard break-up in which the person was the Enchanter, the Renouncer arrives: “never again”. Then someone very bright appears, and this time the person turns out to be the Captive. From outside it looks like three different people. In fact it is three places on one card. Waite has already said why none of them is free. The one on the altar is “also a bondsman”. The Captive holds on too: “I’ll be lost without you” is a chain as well, just one put on someone else. The Renouncer has put it on themselves and calls it principles. The popular feeling of a “sleeping giant” lives exactly here: the strength is there, but it has been locked away so that it can’t do any harm.

The tail also has a sly property: it hands out roles. People who enjoy being held gather quickly around an Enchanter. Couples where one decides everything and the other “can’t do anything without him”. A mentor whose students cannot leave. A manager without whom the team doesn’t make a single decision. A parent around whom a grown-up family revolves. A person with 18-6-15 is often surrounded by people who “can’t manage without them”, gets tired of them — and still doesn’t let go.

sections.h2: The hidden fourth card: everyone with 18-6-15 has the Empress at the centre
paragraphs: Everyone with the 18-6-15 tail has 3, the Empress, at the centre of the matrix. This is not a coincidence but arithmetic: the sum 15 always gives the centre 15 + 15 = 30 → 3. Apart from 18-6-15, only one tail out of 26 has the Empress at the centre — 9-15-6, and it too contains the Lovers and the Devil.

In the method, the centre of the chart is the comfort zone: the state a person returns to when nothing is asked of them. For 18-6-15 that state is abundance. Being liked and being desired. Beauty, pleasure, good food, gifts, care. Being the one who makes everyone feel good. Waite calls the Empress “the Earthly Paradise”, “the fruitful mother of thousands” and “universal fecundity”. Wen writes of her almost as of a magician: “She produces. She makes things happen.” Wen’s Empress “can harness the laws of nature in her favor” and has “an incredible gift for harnessing interpersonal relationships to yield success and harmony”.

The most precise thing in Waite is a single line. Among the images of the Empress, he gives this one too: she has been correctly described as **“desire and the wings thereof”**. And of the Devil he writes: **“the chain and fatality of the material life”**. We read this as one force described twice. At the centre of the tail is desire with wings. At the root is desire in chains. The Devil, by the way, has wings too, “like those of a bat”. But he stands on an altar and flies nowhere.
From this comes our reading: in the 18-6-15 tail, two kinds of magic collide.

**The Empress’s magic is to make things grow.** A gardener doesn’t pull a shoot upwards to make it grow faster. They create the conditions: water, light, soil, time. Everything grows by itself. And what has grown leaves the garden: that is what a harvest is for. The Empress doesn’t hold on; she gives.
**The Devil’s magic is to hold on.** So that it stays. So that it doesn’t leave. So that it is mine.

The tail swings between them. At the centre of the chart, the comfortable thing is to give: to be liked, to care, to shower with gifts. The root fear is that those who received will leave. And then the gift turns into a hook. A present after which you can’t say no. Help after which you can’t leave. Love that has to be paid for with loyalty for ever.
The formulas of the tail add up to a short story:

ul: **The Empress = the Devil + the Devil** (15 + 15 = 30 → 3).
**The Moon = the Devil + the Empress** (15 + 3 = 18).
**The Lovers = the Devil + the Moon** (15 + 18 = 33 → 6).
**The Lovers = the Empress + the Empress** (3 + 3 = 6). This formula shows up in the chakra map: everyone with this tail has Manipura 3-3-6.

paragraphs: What follows is our reading, not a rule of the method. Desire, doubled, gives abundance. The Devil’s strength is not evil in itself. In Waite’s divinatory list this card comes with a proviso: “that which is predestined but is not for this reason evil”. Desire invested in beauty and abundance gives birth to spells. That is where the Moon in this tail comes from: charm is the Empress wanting something very badly. Desire that has passed through spells becomes infatuation. This is the first road to the Lovers, and the scenario follows it: a love born of spells that then has to be held on to.

But a second road leads to the same Lovers: the Empress plus the Empress. Two abundances, two gardens. This is love from fullness, not from spells: the two don’t need to hold each other, because each has a garden of their own. The whole task of the tail fits into one line: **reach the same Lovers by the second road**.

And one last thing. Describing the Empress, Waite also calls her “refugium peccatorum”, the refuge of sinners. For the author of the deck, the central card of the tail called the “Dark Magician” is a refuge for those who have gone wrong. This tail always has a way back. The centre of the chart here is not an altar but a garden.

sections.h2: Where else the tail sounds: Manipura 3-3-6, the Moon in the love line and the Magician for January births
paragraphs: The tail’s arithmetic places its cards in other parts of the matrix too. Here is what everyone who has it shares, without exception:

head: Where in the matrix
What everyone with 18-6-15 has
rows: 3-3-6 — The Empress, The Empress, The Lovers
3 · The Empress — for everyone born from January to July (92% of holders)

paragraphs: An honest caveat: the Svadhisthana energy and the entry to the relationship line are the same point M, and the Muladhara energy is the same point D. The method reads these points in several places. That doesn’t turn them into new coincidences, but it does show where the tail sounds.

**Svadhisthana: joy through the Moon.** In the row of joy and creativity, everyone has the Moon as energy. Joy lives in imagination, in mystery, in a play of images: a costume, a stage, a late-night conversation, the feeling of being watched. The risk is that the pleasure starts to come not from the thing itself but from the impression you make.

**Muladhara: standing on the Devil.** In the row of body, support and matter, everyone has the Devil as energy. The support here is strong desire and a firm grip. In Waite’s divinatory list the Devil has “extraordinary efforts” and “force”. Such a person knows how to get things, keep them and stand firmly on the ground. The risk is that whatever holds you becomes your support: habits, comfort, things, money, people. This is not a diagnosis or a prediction of addiction; the numbers know nothing about that. But if something already has a hold on you, this is the place to start.

**Manipura 3-3-6: will through generosity.** Two Empresses and the Lovers. A person’s will and status show through abundance and care, through the ability to make others feel good, and through partnership. Money often comes through people and relationships. The risk is that generosity turns into power: “I pay, so I decide”, a gift as a leash, the status of someone nobody can do without. The strong version is generosity without a receipt.

**Relationship line: the Moon at the entry, the rest depends on the year of birth.** The tail’s entry, point M, also opens the relationship line. So for everyone with 18-6-15, love begins with the Moon: with enchantment, guesswork and an image. The rest of the line, and the money line along with it, depends only on the year of birth:

For 85% of holders, the relationship line is built the same way: the Moon, then the same card twice. The reason is arithmetic: adding 18 to any number from 5 to 11 gives back the same number. Our reading: in love, the Moon works as a mirror. A person with this tail meets their own reflection in a partner — the one they charmed and what they charmed them with. It helps to ask yourself now and then whom you love right now: the person, or your own reflection in them.

Along the way, the table shows a curious coincidence. For people born in 2001, 2010, 2019 and 2028, the relationship line is 18-6-6 — the same numbers as the “Love Magic” tail. For those born in 1959, 1968, 1977, 1986, 1995, 2004, 2013 and 2022, the relationship line is 18-9-9 (“the Wizard”) and the money line is 9-18-9 (“the Magical Sacrifice”). And for those born in 1989, 1998, 2007, 2016 and 2025, the money line again holds the Devil and the Empress: 12-15-3. These triples should be read through the roles of their own lines, not as a second tail. But the theme of magic in the “Dark Magician” sounds here as well.
**Talent line: the Magician for January births.** The personal talent line B–P–K of people with 18-6-15 depends only on the month of birth:

For those born in January — one holder in five — talent begins with the Magician: 1-5-4, the Magician, the Hierophant and the Emperor. Our reading: the “Dark Magician” has a light one in his talent line. Waite’s Magician stands for the “possession and communication” of the gifts of the Spirit, a light that flows from above to below. His divinatory list has “skill, diplomacy, address, subtlety” — the same charm, but as mastery rather than a chain. And the Hierophant is the very one whose blessing the Devil turns upside down. What works as a spell in the tail stands as a gift in the talent of those born in January. For people born in June the talent line is 6-15-9: the Lovers, the Devil and the Hermit. Here the two lower cards of the tail become a talent: understanding desire and attachment from the inside.

**Purpose: the same four cards.** For 420 of the 843 dates with this tail — almost every second holder — the four points of purpose (personal, social, spiritual and planetary) are 3, 15, 18 and 6. These are exactly the cards of the tail together with the centre: the Empress, the Devil, the Moon and the Lovers. The rest have purpose 3-6-9-15 (356 dates) or 12-6-18-6 (67 dates). Our reading: the cards of this tail are not only a debt but also the material a person is made of. Purpose and scenario are assembled from the same parts. The difference is what you build from them: a garden or a cage.

sections.h2: A parable: Faust, Margarete and the chain around her neck
paragraphs: The parallel below is ours, not part of the method’s tradition. But if you look in literature for a story where magic, love and a pact with the devil meet, you don’t have to look far. It is Goethe’s Faust.

**The Moon.** The tragedy begins at night. The scholar Faust sits in his study and confesses: “That is why I have given myself to magic.” The first thing he turns to is the full moon: “O full moonlight, if only you were looking on my pain for the last time.” The way into the story is night, the moon and magic.

**The Devil.** Faust’s pact with Mephistopheles is a wager about holding on. If Faust ever says the famous words to a passing moment, “Stay, moment, you are so beautiful!”, then, he says, “you may cast me in chains”. The Devil wins the moment a person wants to hold on to something beautiful. The root of the 18-6-15 tail in a single line.

**The Lovers by moonlight.** In the witch’s kitchen, Faust sees a woman’s image in a magic mirror and cannot tear himself away: “That woman’s image was far too beautiful!” Then he drinks a potion, and Mephistopheles mutters: “With this drink inside you, you’ll soon see Helen in every woman.” Love comes in through a reflection in a mirror and a potion — that is the tail’s Moon. Then Gretchen appears (her full name is Margarete). Faust truly loves her. But he acts through Mephistopheles, who slips a box of jewels into the girl’s cupboard. Mephistopheles names the aim outright: “to turn the sweet young thing to your heart’s wish and will”. That is the very definition of a love spell. Gretchen opens the box, tries on a piece and asks: “How would this chain suit me?” In German the word is Kette, which means both a chain you wear and a chain that binds. Remember the Devil card: in Waite, the chains run to the necks.

**The chain.** Everyone knows how it ends. Faust gives Gretchen a vial of sleeping draught so that she can put her mother to sleep before their meeting, and the mother dies. Gretchen herself, who drowned her baby in despair, sits in prison in chains, waiting for execution. Faust comes with Mephistopheles to save her. Her chains fall away. “Just one step, and you are free!” Faust urges. But Gretchen does not go: “Let go! No, I will not suffer force!” Seeing Mephistopheles, she says to Faust: “Heinrich! I am afraid of you.” Mephistopheles announces: “She is condemned!” A voice from above replies: “She is saved!” Our reading: freedom offered by the same means that chained you is a new chain. Liberation begins when you refuse the means that holds.

**The liberty of service.** At the very end of the second part, the old, blind Faust says the line that became a proverb in Russian in Kholodkovsky’s translation: “He alone deserves freedom and life who must win them every day anew!” And he dreams of standing “on free ground with a free people”. Only then does he allow himself the fatal words: to this moment he could say “stay”. Mephistopheles is sure he has won, but he loses: angels carry off Faust’s soul, and one of the penitents, “once called Gretchen”, pleads for him. The only moment a magician can say “stay” without ending up in chains is the moment he sees others free. Waite called this “the liberty of service”.

**A Russian answer.** Bulgakov took lines from Faust as the epigraph to The Master and Margarita: “...who are you, then? — I am part of that power which eternally wills evil and eternally works good.” He gave his heroine the same name as Goethe’s. And Frieda, whom Margarita meets at Woland’s ball, has Gretchen’s story: a seduced girl, a child she killed in despair, eternal punishment. Margarita becomes a witch for the sake of love. The chapter about her flight over Moscow opens with the words: “Invisible and free!” That is the Moon’s freedom — the freedom of someone nobody can see. Then she is given the right to one wish, and she does not spend it on herself: “I want Frieda to stop being given that handkerchief she smothered her baby with.” She explains it like this: Frieda “believes in my power”. Woland says of mercy that it “sometimes creeps, quite unexpectedly and perfidiously, through the narrowest cracks”. And the novel ends with the cry of the Master as he sets Pilate free: “Free! Free! He is waiting for you!”

The same three cards: night magic, love, a pact with a power that “eternally wills evil”. But the power received is spent on letting go. That is the root task of 18-6-15. We won’t bend biographies to fit numbers: by this scheme, Goethe and Bulgakov themselves have a different tail, 18-3-12. What matches is not the person but the plot.
The scenes below are made-up examples, not a description of everyone with this tail.
Most often people recognise the tail by four plots.

**Fast enchantment.** Two weeks after meeting, the other person is sure that nobody has ever understood them like this. A person with 18-6-15 knows how to be a perfect reflection: to be interested in what interests the other, to laugh at their jokes, to say what they need to hear. It is not necessarily calculation. More often it is an instinct that works by itself.

**Being indispensable.** Help, money, connections, problems solved. The partner’s life is arranged so that leaving is unthinkable: too much rests on you. Remember the chain from Mephistopheles’ jewel box. A gift after which you can’t say no is no longer a gift.

**Surveillance.** “Last seen” times, viewed stories, location sharing, three theories about what “ok” means. Jealousy grows not from facts but from what you imagined in the night. The Moon at the entry of the tail gives both intuition and anxiety, and telling one from the other can be very hard.

**The Captive.** The other side of the same tail. A person stays in a relationship that hurts them, because “he’s special”, “nobody ever understood me like this”, “without him I’m nothing”. They were charmed, and they handed over the keys.

Psychology has a term for this, love bombing: a flood of attention, compliments and gifts at the start of a relationship that later becomes a way to control. The tail does not make a person an abuser and does not promise they will meet one. But if you know this pattern from either side, it is the exact shape of the scenario.

The strong version of the tail in love is that second road to the Lovers. Love from fullness, not from spells. In Waite, the Lovers stand “unveiled before each other”, with no images and nothing to hide behind. For this tail that means three things. Show yourself, not a reflection. Say what you want instead of arranging things so that the other person “works it out on their own”. And one day say, and mean it: “I’m with you because I want to be. And you are free to leave.” After that, whoever stays, stays of their own free will, and that kind of love holds more firmly than any chain.

Here the tail has a real gift. Its main talent is influence: sensing what people want and leading them. It does well wherever you need to understand desire from the inside. That means sales, marketing, advertising, brand work, the stage, film, photography, design, psychology, counselling, teaching, managing people. Popular readings advise people with 18-6-15 to go into psychology, creative work, leadership and counselling, and within the tail’s logic this makes sense. The cards support the idea: in Wen, the Moon is the shaman’s signifier, and the Empress is a gift for leading relationships with people to success. Money, as Manipura 3-3-6 shows, often comes through people.
The traps are the same as in love; only the object changes.

ul: **The teacher nobody leaves.** Picture a coach whose clients have been coming for three years and still can’t make a single decision without him. He sincerely helps and is sincerely proud of how much they need him. But a good teacher is measured not by how many students stayed with him but by how many left and managed on their own.

**The grey eminence.** Power without responsibility: making the decisions behind the back of the person who signs. This is exactly what the tail’s legend is about. The modern version is the person without whom nothing happens in the department, even though on paper they are nobody.
**Money as a leash.** “I pay, so I decide.” Loans to friends after which they can’t say “no”. Gifts that send a bill. Luxury as a way of being desired.

paragraphs: There is a simple test of honest influence. Would your technique still work if the person found out about it? Influence that survives being made public is mastery. Waite describes it in the Magician’s divinatory list: “skill, diplomacy, address”. Influence that needs secrecy is a spell.

Popular readings credit this tail with a split attitude to magic: a burning pull or an almost animal fear. The tail neither obliges you to practise esotericism nor forbids it. But it does have a boundary, and it doesn’t run between “I believe” and “I don’t”. Magic without the other person’s consent — a love spell, a “turning-away” spell, a ritual to “bring him back”, a nightly spread about what he is feeling right now — is the dark magic of the name, with or without candles. The test is simple: does your practice increase someone’s freedom, including your own, or reduce it? A spread about your own choice increases it. A ritual performed on another person reduces it.

The fear of “all this magic” in people with this tail is understandable too. Often it is fear of their own power to influence: “if I start, I won’t stop”. And there is one more side of the Moon. Someone who senses the invisible easily believes that the invisible is working against them. If someone offers, for money, to “lift a curse” or “remove a love spell”, remember: the tail shows no influence acting on you. And money paid to remove a chain that doesn’t exist is already a real chain.

Everyone with this tail has the Devil as their Muladhara energy, and popular readings often write about a tendency to addiction: to food, shopping, gambling, alcohol, relationships. The numbers don’t predict this. The sum of three numbers from your birth date knows nothing about your body or your habits. But the tail’s theme is what holds you, and it helps to know the signs. You can’t give something up for a week without real effort. You hide it. Getting it takes more out of you than having it gives back. It no longer brings joy; it holds you. Wen writes of the Devil as a “preference for instant gratification over delayed gratification”. If something holds you so tightly that you can’t stop even when it harms you or the people close to you, that is a job not for a matrix reading but for a professional: a psychotherapist, an addiction specialist, a support group. Turning to them is not weakness but exactly the move the tail calls liberation.

A parent with this tail often loves hard and holds tight. “I gave you my whole life.” Control over grown-up children: where were you, who with, why didn’t you call. Gifts with conditions: a flat, but near us; help with money, but with the right to decide. The child as an extension: their successes are my successes, their choices are my choices. All of it comes from love, and all of it is Mephistopheles’ chain.

The strong version is the Empress at the centre of the chart: a garden that children leave and come back to of their own accord. The most honest question for such a parent: can your grown-up child say “no” to you — and still be loved?

sections.h2: Influence or spell, love or captivity, strength or chain: how to tell them apart
paragraphs: Each card of the tail has a sound version and a scenario version. From outside they are easy to confuse.
**Influence or spell (the Moon):**

ul: Do you influence someone so that they feel better, or so that they stay?
Do you show a person what is there, or what they want to see?
Can the other person say no without being punished — without coldness, resentment, withdrawal?
Do you know about their feelings from their words, or from your guesses?

paragraphs: **Love or captivity (the Lovers):**

ul: Next to you, does a person become more like themselves — or more like your idea of them?
Would you choose this relationship again in daylight, knowing everything you know now?
If tomorrow they said “I’m leaving”, what would you feel first: pain, or rage that they dared?
Does each of you have a life, friends and things to do that don’t pass through the other?

paragraphs: **Strength or chain (the Devil):**

ul: Who is holding whom? Answer honestly, about yourself and about the other person.
Could you give this up for a week without much effort?
Does it matter more to you that they are happy, or that they need you?
What do you do when you hear “no”?

paragraphs: **Garden or cage (the Empress):**

ul: Do the people you care for become more independent over time, or more dependent?
Does your generosity send a bill?
Is there someone in your life who once left you for a life of their own — and you are glad of it?

sections.h2: What to do with the 18-6-15 tail: eight practices
paragraphs: These are the author’s exercises, drawn from the logic of the three cards. They are not a ritual and not a promise of results.

ol: **Say out loud why.** Before any act of influence — a compliment, a pause in texting, a gift, a hint, help — ask yourself one question: could I tell this person out loud why I’m doing this? “I’m texting you first because I missed you” — fine. “I’m not texting so that you’ll miss me” — not fine; that is a spell. Waite’s Hierophant raises his hand in blessing, and the Devil, according to Waite, shows the same gesture in reverse. Influence you can speak about out loud is a blessing. Influence you have to hide is its reverse side.

**A gift without a chain.** Before giving money, help or a present, ask yourself: would I give this if the person left my life tomorrow? If yes, it is a gift. If not, it is a Kette, the chain from Mephistopheles’ jewel box. Better not to give it at all than to give it with a hook.

**The right to “no”.** Once a week, give someone a real chance to turn you down: “You don’t have to agree, I won’t be hurt.” And keep your word. The flip side is the same: learn to hear “no” without coldness, resentment or revenge. Love that can survive a refusal is held by choice, not by a chain.

**Help by invitation.** Don’t rescue people who didn’t ask. You can ask once: “Would you like some help?” And accept “no” as the answer. Help nobody asked for is the most polite kind of control. Popular readings give people with this tail exactly this advice, and here they are right.

**Night-time decisions in the morning.** The Moon is strongest in the dark. A message written at two in the morning on a wave of feeling — send it in the morning. A decision to buy, to pick a fight or to break up made in the heat of the moment — put it off for three days. Wen calls the Devil a preference for instant gratification over delayed gratification. The pause between desire and action is where you get to choose for yourself again.

**An inventory of chains.** Divide a sheet of paper into two columns: “what holds me” and “what I hold”. People, habits, things, roles, subscriptions, promises. Next to each item, answer: could I let this go for a week? Where the answer is “no”, there is a link. Start with the smallest link, not the scariest one. Waite reminds us that the chained figures on the card have human faces. A chain does not take away your mind; you can think about it.

**The measure of a garden.** Choose one person you influence: a partner, a child, a student, an employee. This month, do one thing after which they will need you less. Teach them to do for themselves what you have always done for them. The Empress’s magic is measured not by how many people depend on you, but by how many grew up next to you and were able to leave.

**Strength into open work.** In Waite’s divinatory list, the Devil has “extraordinary efforts” and “force”. This strength needs an outlet, or it will go into power over people. Sport, a project, the stage, a business, creative work — something where you can burn, want and strive in the open. And know the limit: if something holds you so tightly that you can’t stop, or if a relationship involves threats and violence, you need professionals, not practices from an article.

paragraphs: And five phrases that break the scenario in the moment:

ul: Instead of “he’ll be lost without me” — “he’ll manage. If he asks, I’ll help.”
Instead of “what if he leaves” — “he may leave. I want him to stay of his own free will.”
Instead of “but I did everything for you” — “I did it because I wanted to. You don’t owe me anything.”
Instead of “I can’t live without him” — “I’m scared to be without him. That’s not the same thing.”
Instead of “I know what’s best for you” — “and what do you want?”

sections.h2: The strength of 18-6-15: a magician who lets go
paragraphs: A worked-through 18-6-15 is a person who makes you want to be better and still lets you leave. Their charm hasn’t gone anywhere. They still sense what people want, know how to inspire, gather people around them and lead. But they do it openly. Their generosity doesn’t send a bill. Their love doesn’t hold, and that is why people don’t leave them. They know the chain from the inside, so they see better than others where someone has love and where a hook, where a teacher and where a guru, where help and where a leash. Such people become the ones who help others get free: psychologists, mentors, the friends people come to when they “can’t leave”.

Wen tells a Buddhist story about the Devil. Mara, who personifies the thirst for pleasure, the thirst for existence and the thirst for power, tempted the Buddha. The Buddha reached down his right hand and touched the earth, asking it to bear witness to his defeat of Mara — the defeat of his own inner demons. On the Devil card the torch also points to the earth, but it burns. The Buddha’s hand touches the earth to call it as a witness. It is the same downward gesture, and the whole work of this tail lies between the two.

Waite left this tail a key in a single phrase. The one who towers over the chained pair is “blind to the liberty of service”. The liberty of service is what a worked-through 18-6-15 sees. Strength that serves someone else’s freedom is the only kind of power that leaves no chains behind. Faust allowed himself to say “stay, moment” only when he pictured a free people on free ground. Margarita spent her wish on someone else’s handkerchief. The Master set Pilate free.
**The Dark Magician holds on. A worked-through 18-6-15 can still enchant, but afterwards opens the door.** And people come back of their own accord.

sections.h2: What this reading is based on

ul: **Calculation** — the classic destiny matrix scheme with points A–T: D = A + B + C, E = A + B + C + D, M = D + E, N = D + M. Relationship line: M–R1–R; money line: L–R2–R, where L = C + E, R = L + M, R1 = M + R, R2 = L + R. Talent line: B–P–K, where K = B + E, P = B + K. Rows of the chakra map: Manipura E–E, Svadhisthana L–M, Muladhara C–D; emotions are the sum of the first two numbers. Purpose: personal is the sum of the sky line (B, D) and the earth line (A, C), social is the sum of the ancestral lines, spiritual is the sum of personal and social, planetary is the sum of social and spiritual. Every sum over 22 is reduced by adding its digits. All numerical facts in this article come from going through all 73,414 dates from 1900 to 2100 on the project’s calculation engine, checked against reference examples. The brute-force check covered the single sum 15, the constant centre 3, Manipura 3-3-6, frequencies by decade, year and month, the matches with the relationship, money and talent lines, the distribution of purposes and the absence of the tail under the “minus 22” rule.

**Card meanings** — A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1910, reissued 1922) and Benebell Wen, Holistic Tarot (2015). Quotations are given in the authors’ original English. Waite’s divinatory meanings come from the third part of his book and are always labelled as his divinatory list, separate from his reading of the symbolism. The comparison of the Magician and the Devil based on Waite’s descriptions is ours.

**Literature** — J. W. von Goethe, Faust (Part One 1808, Part Two 1832). Quotations are translated from the German for this article; in Russian, the line “He alone deserves freedom and life…” is known in N. A. Kholodkovsky’s translation. M. A. Bulgakov, The Master and Margarita, chapters 21, 24 and 32; quotations translated from the Russian. The parallel between both books and the tail is ours.
**Etymology** — from etymological dictionaries of Russian (M. Vasmer and others). The origin of words proves nothing about numbers and is given as an observation about language.

**The name “Dark Magician” and the past-life legend** come from popular interpretations of the destiny matrix. Neither Waite nor Wen wrote about the matrix or karmic tails. Putting the three cards together into a scenario, reading the centre as “a magic that makes things grow”, the Enchanter, Captive and Renouncer modes, and the practices are the author’s interpretation.

This is an esoteric model for self-observation, not a forecast, a diagnosis or advice on health, money or relationships. If a relationship involves threats, violence or coercion, the cause is neither the tail nor you: what is needed here is real help, not work with numbers.

faq.q: What happened in the past life of a person with the 18-6-15 tail?
faq.a: Popular interpretations speak of a magician or priest with secret knowledge who used it for harm: cast love spells, laid curses, bent other people’s will. In other versions it is a “grey eminence” behind a ruler, or someone who lived a life of affairs and love intrigues. This is a legend of the tradition: neither numbers nor cards establish events in past lives. It is more useful to read it as a description of what can already be seen now: a person’s relationship with their own power to influence and with the wish to hold on.

faq.q: Does 18-6-15 mean I’m a sorcerer, or that I’ve been cursed?
faq.a: No. The tail is three numbers derived from a date of birth. It cannot show whether someone performed a ritual on you or you on someone else, and no paid “removal” service changes these numbers. The Devil here is a symbol, not a being. Wen writes plainly that it is “not a literal beast or demon” but a personification of “human selfishness and indulging in that selfishness”. If you feel that you are “being held”, it is more useful to look at real chains: obligations, debts, habits, relationships.

faq.q: Can I practise esotericism and read cards with the 18-6-15 tail?
faq.a: Yes, the tail forbids nothing. Popular readings advise studying esotericism responsibly, without shallow practices or manipulation, and within the tail’s logic this is sensible. There is only one boundary: a practice must not reduce someone else’s freedom. A spread about your own choice is fine. A love spell, a “turning-away” spell, reading the cards every evening about a particular person’s feelings instead of talking to them — that is the very dark side the name refers to.

faq.q: Does the 18-6-15 tail mean I’m a manipulator?
faq.a: No. The tail describes not a character but a scenario that can switch on: charm, a bond, fear of loss, holding on. Many people with 18-6-15 never manipulate consciously. But they often recognise subtle forms of it in themselves: helping in order to be needed; being sad so that someone stays; going quiet so that someone misses them. Noticing this is not a reason to blame yourself but the first step out of the circle. And remember that the tail can also sound from the other side — in the person who is being controlled.

The numbers do not predict addictions and cannot tell whether you have one. But the Devil is the card of what holds you, and everyone with this tail has it in the Muladhara energy, the row of body and support. So the tail’s theme is attachment in general: to people, pleasures, things, money, the role of the indispensable one. If something holds you and harms you or those close to you, you need a professional, not a matrix reading.

Yes, if 15, 6 and 18 are on the bottom ray of your chart: you have simply read the tail from the outer corner towards the centre. In the calculation it is written from the inner point M to the corner D. There is no separate 15-6-18 tail: with 18 in the bottom corner the centre is always 9, and the tail comes out as 9-9-18. The triple 15-6-18 does appear in other lines. It is the relationship line for some people with the 15-20-5 tail and the money line for some people with 3-7-22 and 3-22-19. There it is read through the roles of its own line. In search, both versions are written with spaces: “18 6 15” and “15 6 18”.

All three contain the Lovers, and people often confuse them. 18-6-15 shares its entry and middle with 18-6-6 (“Love Magic”): the Moon and the Lovers. The root and the centre differ. In 18-6-6 the root is the Lovers again and the centre is the Hanged Man: it is a story about loving an image and about waiting, and the task there is to choose. In 18-6-15 the root is the Devil: the task is to free yourself from what already holds you and not to hold anyone yourself. 18-6-15 shares its centre, the Empress, with 9-15-6 (“the World of Passions and Fairy Tales”), along with the same Lovers and Devil, but in reverse order. There the Devil is the mechanism and the Lovers the root: the chain leads back to the choice of love. Here the Lovers are the mechanism and the Devil the root: love seen by the light of the Moon leads to the chain. All three come from different sums: 18-6-15 from 15, 9-15-6 from 24, 18-6-6 from 33, 42 or 51.

faq.q: Why doesn’t another calculator show 18-6-15 for me?
faq.a: It comes down to the reduction rule. In the classic scheme, a sum over 22 is reduced by adding its digits: 23 → 5, 30 → 3. Some calculators subtract 22 instead: 23 → 1, 30 → 8. Under that rule the 18-6-15 tail never occurs at all, for any date from 1900 to 2100. The same dates get other tails there, most often 1-16-15 or 11-22-11. So if one calculator shows you 18-6-15 and another doesn’t, the second one simply uses a different rule. The classic result is easy to check by hand: the day arcanum, the month and the year arcanum must add up to exactly 15.

faq.q: Is 18-6-15 different for women and men?
faq.a: No. Gender plays no part in the calculation, and the meaning of the tail doesn’t depend on it. The images of the “femme fatale” and the “manipulative man” are stereotypes, not arithmetic: charm, jealousy and the wish to hold on are not divided by gender. Anyone can be the Enchanter, the Captive or the Renouncer, and often the same person in different years.

The numbers in the matrix don’t change. What changes is how the scenario plays out. Signs of a worked-through tail: you use your charm openly and can say out loud why you do what you do. Your gifts don’t send a bill. You help when asked and hear “no” without taking revenge. The people you care for become more independent over time. You can leave a relationship where you are being held, and you don’t hold on to those who want to leave. Then the tail stays a description of a strength, not a story that repeats itself.

This question comes up often. It is the tail of a new generation: one in 31 people born since 2000 has it, while among their grandparents, born in the 1950s, it is one in 126. In 2026 it fell on only five dates: 4 and 31 January, 3 February, 2 March and 1 April. In 2027 it will fall on four: 3 and 30 January, 2 February and 1 March. Such a child especially needs three things. The first: charm should not become a way of getting things. They will learn early that a smile and tears can get them a lot. Don’t punish this, but don’t reward it either. Respond to a direct request more readily than to a manoeuvre. The second: the right to “no” in both directions. Let them be able to refuse you, and let them hear a refusal from you calmly, without being punished by withdrawn love. The third: the ability to wait. The Devil at the root is instant gratification, so sweets after dinner, games after homework and a present on the birthday rather than right away are not cruelty but training in freedom. And watch your own chains. A child who is loved on conditions learns to love the same way.

report: Russian speaks of love in a sorcerer’s vocabulary. Ocharovat, to charm, comes from chary, “spells”. Privorozhit, to win with a love spell, from vorozhit, “to work magic”. Prelstit, to seduce, from lest, which once meant “deceit”. Plenit, to captivate, from plen, “captivity”; privyazannost, attachment, from privyazat, “to tie up”. Popular readings call 18-6-15 the “Dark Magician”: in the legend, someone in a past life used secret knowledge to cast love spells and bend others’ will. The legend cannot be checked; numbers are silent about past lives. But this tail needs no candles. It already lies in ordinary words about love: spells are the Moon at the entry, love the Lovers in the middle, captivity and the tether the Devil at the root.

Etymology proves nothing about numbers. But it shows that the dark magic here is no occult gift but an ordinary human one: being liked, drawing people in, staying on someone’s mind. Yet the cards hold magic too. Among Waite’s divinatory meanings for the Moon are “darkness”, “deception” and “occult forces”. Benebell Wen calls the Moon the signifier for society’s “magi, priest, or shaman”: the moon pulls on the water, and when the card appears in a reading, an “external invisible force” pulls on the person. A spell is exactly that: an invisible pull.

report.h3: The one who holds the chain is chained too

report: Waite’s key line about the Devil is not about magic. He describes a man and a woman chained to the altar, “as if Adam and Eve after the Fall”. And then: “he who is exalted above them is not to be their master for ever. Even now, he is also a bondsman, sustained by the evil that is in him and blind to the liberty of service.” **The dark magician of the legend is the least free figure on his own card.** The one who holds is held.

In passing, Waite praises the deck of Papus, where this card shows not demons but a man and a woman “yoked only to each other”. A chain needs no third party: the bond between two can itself become the chain.

report.h3: Loved for a reflection — and reflections break

report: The circle starts with instinct. A person with 18-6-15 reads a room in a second, sees what someone is missing — and becomes it. For Waite the Moon is “life of the imagination apart from life of the spirit”, and the way is lit by “only reflected light”. The other falls in love with the reflection, not the person. The light falls both ways: whoever charms easily is just as easily charmed.

Wen writes of the Lovers: “a strong feeling of paradise, at least in the beginning” — but “under every flower a serpent coiled”. In a moonlit union both chose an image, and the person with this tail suspects as much. So the union has to be guarded rather than lived. Where fear of loss lives, chains appear: control, jealousy over things imagined, help with a hook, rescue nobody asked for.

A woman of twenty-four meets a man, and within an hour she knows what he is missing: being understood. She gives him that. Six months later she knows his schedule, has rewritten his CV and lent him money for a course. When he plans a weekend away with friends, she forbids nothing. She just gets sad, and he stays. One day he says he lives under a glass dome with her. She answers that she did everything for him. **That is true — and that is the chain.**

The same tail may be his — the one who stays while suffocating, because “nobody has ever understood me like this”. The Enchanter holds: “he’ll be lost without me”. The Captive clings: “I can’t leave”. And there is a third, the Renouncer: “I don’t need anyone” — a chain put on oneself and called principles. These are not three people but three places on one card.

report.h3: Desire with wings, desire in chains

report: Everyone with this tail has the Empress at the centre of the chart — the comfort zone: being liked, caring, giving gifts. Waite has a line the whole tail rests on: the Empress has been correctly described as “desire and the wings thereof”. Of the Devil he writes: “the chain and fatality of the material life”. We read this as one force described twice: at the centre, desire with wings; at the root, desire in chains.

Hence two kinds of magic. The Empress makes things grow: a gardener never pulls a shoot upwards but gives it water and light, and the harvest leaves the garden — that is what it is for. The Devil holds on: so that it stays, so that it is mine. Giving feels good, but those who receive might leave — and the gift turns into a hook. A present that makes refusal impossible. Help that makes leaving impossible.

Goethe showed this most precisely (the parallel is ours, not the method’s). Faust loves Gretchen but acts through Mephistopheles, who slips her a box of jewels. Gretchen tries on a piece: “How would this chain suit me?” In German, Kette means both a necklace and a chain that binds.

Our reading from here: in this tail two roads lead to the Lovers. The first is the Devil plus the Moon (15 + 18 = 33 → 6): a love born of spells that must then be held on to. The scenario takes this one. The second is the Empress plus the Empress (3 + 3 = 6): two gardens, love from fullness, where neither needs to hold the other. The tail’s whole task is to **reach the same Lovers by the second road**.

One question separates a gift from a spell: would the technique still work if the person found out? Influence that survives exposure is mastery; in Waite’s list for the Magician it is “skill, diplomacy, address”. Influence that needs secrecy is a spell. The practices below are the author’s, not a ritual or a promise of results:

ul: say out loud why: texting first “because I missed him” is fine, going silent “so that he’ll miss me” is already a spell;
give only what would still be given if the person left tomorrow — otherwise it is a Kette;
help only when invited: help nobody asked for is the most polite kind of control;
leave night-time decisions until morning: the Moon is strongest in the dark.

report: If something holds so tightly that stopping is impossible, or a relationship involves threats and violence, it takes a professional — a psychotherapist, an addiction specialist, a support group — not a matrix reading.

report.h3: The magician who opens the door

report: A worked-through 18-6-15 is someone next to whom people want to be better — and are still free to leave. The charm stays but works in the open, and the generosity sends no bill. They know the chain from the inside and see better than most where there is love and where a hook. Their magic is measured not by how many people depend on them but by how many grew alongside them and were able to leave.

Waite left this tail a key in a single phrase: the one above the chained pair is “blind to the liberty of service”. Strength that serves someone else’s freedom is the only power that leaves no chains behind. **The Dark Magician holds on. A worked-through 18-6-15 can still enchant, but afterwards opens the door.** And people come back of their own accord.
